title: Proposal of the name, Orangeburg Group, for outcropping beds of Eocene age in Orangeburg County and vicinity, South Carolina
citation: Siple, G.E., and Pooser, W.K., 1975, Proposal of the name, Orangeburg Group, for outcropping beds of Eocene age in Orangeburg County and vicinity, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Bulletin 1395-A [p. A55].
notes:
Citation scope: the PDF is all of USGS Bulletin 1395-A (Changes in stratigraphic nomenclature, 1973). This record is only the Siple and Pooser paper on p. A55 (PDF page 61, in packet-02). This packet (PDF pages 1-51) holds the bulletin front matter and the Cohee and Wright listing of nomenclatural changes for the whole country, plus the Scott (Colorado) and Sims and Sarna-Wojcicki (California) papers; it includes listing entries summarizing the Orangeburg Group change (e.g. PDF p. 37), but those are not the record's paper, so no values are recorded.
Citation scope: the record is the Siple and Pooser paper, which occupies only PDF page 61 (bulletin p. A55) of the whole Bulletin 1395-A PDF. Values come only from page 61, plus the three references the paper cites (Cooke 1936, Cooke and MacNeil 1952, Dall 1898) taken from the bulletin's shared reference list (PDF pp. 66-67). Other pages of this packet (end of the Sims and Sarna-Wojcicki California paper, the Weir Kentucky paper, rest of the shared reference list) are not recorded. The paper gives no thicknesses, localities beyond counties, borings or structures.

description.value: Name Orangeburg reinstated for USGS usage, raised in rank to group status, and restricted to Orangeburg and surrounding counties in South Carolina; consists of the Congaree Formation, Warley Hill Marl, and restricted McBean Formation of Claiborne age and the Barnwell Formation of Jackson age in their outcrop areas in northwestern Orangeburg County; used in lieu of Jackson and Claiborne Groups
description.quote: The name Orangeburg is herein reinstated for usage by the U.S. Geological Survey, raised in rank to group status, and restricted to Orangeburg and surrounding counties in South Carolina.
